issues.title: 11000213: compact Veech-group obstructions; existence unresolved
issues.body:
This attempt leaves the compact purely cyclic Veech-group existence question unresolved. It proves that a finite translation cover of a torus, branched over a finite set invariant under a hyperbolic affine map, retains two noncommuting parabolic derivatives. It also isolates the compactness and unmarked-realization gaps in transferring the known noncompact finite-area construction.

The full compact/projective derivative-group target, classical attribution, and current-source qualifications are retained. Two substantive approaches were used; recommended status is unsolved 2/5.

Separate adversarial review passed the unchanged proof with no corrections. The 7,854 author assertions reproduce byte-for-byte, and all 16,415 independent exact controls pass, including actual unbased-cover class permutations and lift relabellings. These controls accompany the written covering-space proof and do not certify a compact example. AI-reviewed and unrefereed; no priority claim.

issues.title: Prove the labelled sine ratio for short polygon trajectories (5000006)
issues.body:
This gives a complete candidate proof of Fuchs’s Conjecture 2.7: parallel short trajectories of types A_k and A_l have the proposed sine length ratio, for every regular n-gon with n>=3.

The proof identifies the source’s parity-sensitive type through cone-germ angles on the double polygon, proves affine invariance using the hyperelliptic involution in the even case, and applies credited classical Veech cusp reduction. The triangular, square and hexagonal marked-vertex cases are handled separately. It preserves the source’s dihedral meaning of parallelism and does not assume or claim neighbouring conjectures.

Separate adversarial AI review passed without correction. All 14,630 submitted exact assertions reproduced byte for byte; 60,055 independent exact controls passed. The mathematical snapshot is unchanged, with its historical pending-review header explained in the README.

The original Veech full text was not retrieved: the precise imported group and cusp statements were checked in full primary papers by Finster and Boulanger–Lanneau–Massart, with that limitation explicit. This is AI-reviewed, unrefereed work; historical priority is unconfirmed.

One substantive attempt was used. Only the problem’s attempt folder is changed; the parent workflow will update the queue.

issues.title: Prove the signed parallel-trajectory type rule (5000005)
issues.body:
This restores a complete proof candidate for Fuchs's Conjecture 2.6: at slope ell*pi/n + epsilon*alpha, the short-trajectory type is A_(epsilon*k-ell), with indices modulo n-2 and even ell when n is even. It includes all n>=3, side boundaries, existence of the first-vertex endpoint, and the full source's segment-parity convention.

The new step is a common cyclic labelling of outgoing and backward endpoint germs. Model chords pair these labels by a reflection; one affine map transports the matching by a common shift. Angular alignment gives 2a=ell without dividing by two modulo an even modulus. The neighboring cone/type work in PR152 is credited; its length-ratio result is not assumed.

Separate adversarial AI review returned PASS_COMPLETE_SIGNED_TYPE_RULE with no mandatory mathematical correction. The author checker replayed all 3,276,822 exact assertions; 441,920 independently authored exact controls passed. The frozen mathematical proof is unchanged and the full review artifacts are included.

Classical Veech group/cusp theorems are imported and credited. Their precise statements were checked in complete primary papers by Finster and Boulanger–Lanneau–Massart; the original Veech1989 full text was not retrieved. This is AI-reviewed, unrefereed work, with no historical-priority claim.

The interrupted route is preserved: one historical turn plus one reconstruction response gives 2/5 consumed author turns and one approach family. The missing original candidate is not represented as identical-byte recovery. Only this problem's attempt folder and its QUEUE.md row are in scope.
